section: C.2 Rectangular OLEE Prior Collapse and Detached-Prior Optimization
text:
C.2 Rectangular OLEE Prior Collapse and Detached-Prior Optimization
A structural distinction separates square ambient-space normalizing flows (Flow-SiMR, where \(f_{\text{flow},m}: \mathbb{R}^{p_m} \to \mathbb{R}^{p_m}\), stabilized with bounded coupling scales scale_bound = 0.5, optional Probabilistic PCA base distributions base_distribution="gaussian_pca", and exact likelihood-preserving post-flow shared \(\mathrm{O}(k)\) Varimax gauge rotations varimax=True (Kaiser 1958)) from rectangular OLEE-bottlenecked flows (Flow-SiMR-V, where \(\mathbf{V}_m \in \mathbb{R}^{p_m \times k}\) with \(k \ll p_m\) precedes \(f_{\text{flow},m}: \mathbb{R}^k \to \mathbb{R}^k\)).

C.2.1 Why End-to-End Gaussian Prior Gradients Collapse \(\mathbf{V}_m\)
In standard normalizing flows, maximum likelihood training minimizes the negative log-likelihood under a standard isotropic Gaussian prior \(p(\mathbf{z}) = \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I}_k)\): \[
\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}; f_{\text{flow},m}) = \frac{1}{2n}\sum_{i=1}^n \|f_{\text{flow},m}(\mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin},i})\|_2^2 - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i=1}^n \log \left|\det \frac{\partial f_{\text{flow},m}}{\partial \mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin}}}(\mathbf{z}_{m,\text{lin},i})\right|.
\] When the rectangular projection \(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}} = \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m\) (\(k \ll p_m\)) precedes the flow, the change-of-variables determinant \(\log |\det J_{f_{\text{flow},m}}|\) accounts only for volume changes inside the \(k\)-dimensional subspace and contains no log-determinant term for the rectangular projection \(\mathbf{V}_m\). If \(\nabla_{\mathbf{V}_m} \mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}\) is backpropagated into \(\mathbf{V}_m\), the quadratic penalty \(\frac{1}{2}\|\mathbf{Z}_m\|_2^2 = \frac{1}{2}\operatorname{tr}(\mathbf{V}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m) + \mathcal{O}(\|f_{\text{flow},m} - \mathrm{id}\|)\) is minimized by rotating \(\mathbf{V}_m\) onto the trailing eigenvectors of \(\mathbf{X}_m^\top \mathbf{X}_m\) with the smallest eigenvalues \(\lambda_{p_m-k+1}, \dots, \lambda_{p_m}\).


C.2.2 Detached-Prior Subspace-Decoupled Optimization
To prevent rectangular prior collapse, Flow-SiMR-V detaches \(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}\) at the input to the Gaussian prior penalty:

OLEE basis update (\(\mathbf{V}_m\)): Updated exclusively by the cross-view alignment energy \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{align}}\) and within-view relative reconstruction loss \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}}\), while detaching \(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}\) in the prior term (\(\operatorname{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}) = \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}.\text{detach}()\)).
Bijective flow update (\(f_{\text{flow},m}\)): Trained via \(\mathcal{L}_{\text{NLL}}(f_{\text{flow},m}(\operatorname{sg}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}))) + \mathcal{L}_{\text{align}} + \mathcal{L}_{\text{recon}}\), initialized with zero scale and translation weights (\(s_\ell = 0, t_\ell = 0\)) at epoch \(0\) so \(f_{\text{flow},m}^{(0)}(\mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}) = \mathbf{Z}_{m,\text{lin}}\).

In the ADNI-MCI hyperparameter sweep (\(N = 1,084\), \(k = 3\), Protocol B, 1,025 configurations), the best Flow-SiMR-V configuration reaches an out-of-sample CogPC1 \(R^2\) of 0.2686; across the 3-seed benchmark its linear score on ADNI-MCI is 0.198, and its mean Friedman rank on the linear probe over all 12 datasets is 3.58.

C.3.1 Conditional Clinical Imputation (True vs. Imputed Serums)
Because Flow-SiMR-V preserves invertibility on the \(k\)-dimensional bottleneck space, it supports conditional cross-view inference via the Gaussian Schur complement in post-flow latent space (pysimlr.predict_conditional_view). In Figure C.1, we train Flow-SiMR-V on the Diabetes dataset under a leak-free 70/30 split, withhold the blood serum view on test patients, and evaluate serum triglyceride (s5) imputation from vitals alone via pysimlr.plot_predictions.








Figure C.1: Flow-SiMR-V conditional Schur-complement decoding (pysimlr.predict_conditional_view) imputes held-out serum triglycerides (s5) from systemic vitals alone (pysimlr.plot_predictions). Points show observed versus imputed training-standardized s5 on the 30% held-out Diabetes test split (\(k = 2\)), with the solid line marking identity and the header reporting test correlation and error.







C.3.2 Flow Warping, Stacked Term Convergence, and Dynamic Modality Weights
To audit how the downstream normalizing flow transforms the linear first-layer projection \(\mathbf{X}_m \mathbf{V}_m \mathbf{R}\) into the aligned latent coordinates \(\mathbf{Z}_m \mathbf{R}\), Figure C.2 applies pysimlr.plot_flow_warping on Diabetes (\(k = 2\), dynamic_weights=True): monotone binned median traces and high Spearman \(\rho\) confirm that the coupling layers bend densities smoothly without folding or inverting the sign semantics of \(\mathbf{V}_m\). Figure C.3 and Figure C.4 display the corresponding stacked objective-term trajectories (pysimlr.plot_convergence, separating total loss, cross-view similarity, and reconstruction onto independent scales without secondary axes) and degree-of-freedom-corrected MAI view weights (pysimlr.plot_modality_weights).








Figure C.2: Downstream normalizing flow coupling layers preserve the directional sign ordering of the linear entrypoint on the two-view Diabetes cohort (pysimlr.plot_flow_warping, flow_v, \(k = 2\)). Figure C.3: Flow-SiMR-V optimization converges smoothly across total loss, cross-view similarity alignment, and relative reconstruction (pysimlr.plot_convergence, stacked three-panel diagnostic separating terms onto independent vertical scales).

C.3.3 Input-Boundary Feature Structure Across Three Cardiovascular Views
Prepending \(\mathbf{V}_m\) preserves direct feature-level interpretability across downstream normalizing flow coupling layers. Figure C.5 displays pysimlr.plot_top_features across the three views of the Heart cohort (flow_v, \(k = 2\)).

C.3.4 Latent Trajectory Interpolation
Tracing a straight-line interpolation in the shared latent space between a low-risk and high-risk patient and inverting it through \(f_{\text{flow},m}^{-1}\) and \(\mathbf{V}_m^\top\) defines a smooth trajectory in feature space (Figure C.6).

Decoded biomarker trajectories along a straight-line latent interpolation path between Patient #0 (low-risk, \(\alpha = 0.0\)) and Patient #10 (high-risk, \(\alpha = 1.0\)) on the Diabetes cohort (\(k = 2\)). Colored trajectories track Body Mass Index (bmi, blue circles), Blood Pressure (bp, orange squares), and Age (age, green triangles) decoded through \(f_{\text{flow},0}^{-1}\) and \(\mathbf{V}_0^\top\).

D.2 Non-Parametric Benchmark Engine and Optimization Stack
All statistical hypothesis tests, ranking matrices, and permutation null distributions are computed by src/pysimlr/benchmarks/deep_ranking.py:

Non-parametric Friedman omnibus test (Friedman 1937) and Iman–Davenport \(F\)-distribution extension (Demšar 2006; Iman and Davenport 1980).
Two-tailed Nemenyi Critical Difference (\(CD =\) 2.600 at \(\alpha = 0.05\) for \(k =\) 7, \(B =\) 12) (Nemenyi 1963; Demšar 2006).
Pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests (Wilcoxon 1945) with Holm–Bonferroni step-down adjustments (Holm 1979).
Adaptive first-order (Adam, AdamW (Kingma and Ba 2015; Loshchilov and Hutter 2019)) and Riemannian manifold solvers implemented on top of PyTorch (Paszke et al. 2019), NumPy (Harris et al. 2020), SciPy (Virtanen et al. 2020), and Scikit-Learn (Pedregosa et al. 2011).
Benchmark cohorts span clinical cardiology (Heart (Detrano et al. 1989)), metabolic progression (Diabetes (Efron et al. 2004)), handwritten pattern descriptors (mfeat (Breukelen et al. 1998)), transcriptomic/multi-omic cancer benchmarks (Golub et al. 1999; The Cancer Genome Atlas Network 2012; The Cancer Genome Atlas Research Network 2013; Wang et al. 2014; Tenenhaus and Tenenhaus 2011; Tenenhaus et al. 2014; Zhao et al. 2017; Abdi et al. 2013), and Alzheimer’s neuroimaging (ADNI-MCI (Mueller et al. 2005; Jack et al. 2008; Weiner et al. 2017)).

The test suites tests/test_deep_ranking_stats.py and tests/test_implementation_standards.py verify the statistical calculations and package standards:
pytest tests/test_deep_ranking_stats.py tests/test_implementation_standards.py -v

D.3.1 Block-Level Sign-Flip Permutation Floor
In paired comparisons across \(B =\) 12 independent dataset blocks (where each block cell is the mean across \(N_{\text{seeds}} =\) 3 replicates (Demšar 2006)), the exact distribution-free sign-flip null distribution across the \(B =\) 12 blocks consists of \(2^B = 4,096\) sign assignments:
\[
p_{\text{perm}} = \frac{1}{2^B} \sum_{\mathbf{s} \in \{-1, +1\}^B} \mathbb{I}\left(\left|\frac{1}{B} \sum_{i=1}^B s_i \Delta_i\right| \ge |\bar{\Delta}|\right), \qquad p_{\min, B=12} = \frac{2}{2^{12}} = \frac{2}{4096} \approx 0.000488
\]


D.3.2 v0.43.1 Replication Designs and Provenance Ledger

Synthetic Propositions and Design A/B Benchmark (v043_synthetic_theorems.json): scripts/benchmark_synthetic_theorems.py evaluates 20 random seeds (\(N_{\text{train}} =\) 60, \(N_{\text{test}} =\) 200, view dimensions (80, 100, 60, 160)) with paired two-sided Wilcoxon signed-rank tests across arms.
Six-Cohort Real-Data Revisit (part_a_*, part_b_*): scripts/run_real_data_v043.py evaluates Part A (108 simlr fits across 6 real cohorts \(\times\) 3 seeds, yielding 81 matched comparisons across 27 pre-v0.43 cells in part_a_simlr_v043_raw.csv and part_a_comparison_summary.csv) and Part B (96 fit_uniform_shrunk fits: 48 conical and 48 radial-convex across 6 cohorts \(\times k \in \{1, 2, 3\} \times\) 3 seeds in part_b_uniform_shrunk_raw.csv and part_b_uniform_shrunk_summary.csv).
Audit Evidence and Provenance Ledger (docs/audit/evidence/): Supporting design evidence tables record 20-subsample rank selection (adni_rank_selection.csv), two-stage default selection (default_selection_stage1.csv, 1,664 fits; default_selection_stage2.csv, 180 fits across 20 cells), scale-free view weighting (view_weighting_acc.csv), collapse threshold selection (collapse_threshold_selection.csv), unpenalized deep collapse (deep_collapse_diagnosis.csv), and deep convergence consistency (deep_default_consistency.csv, 18 runs per family).
